blocks: ### Phase 4 - Mode A and the page writer (Story 4, P4)

decisions.summary: Phase 1 planned to the task; phases 2-4 to their approach, each planned to the task when it opens by a reviewed plan amendment.
decisions.why: Sequencing of planning, not of scope; every phase stays in FR-001's order and every later plan amendment is reviewed.

decisions.summary: serde_json is the one crate phase 1 adds; further crates named per phase.
decisions.why: Implementation choice the request and spec leave open; narrows nothing asked.

decisions.id: TC / Structure - Cargo workspace, a crate per phase
decisions.summary: rust/guard beside rust/phases in one workspace, make rust-test/lint/cover over both.
decisions.why: Layout decision; FR-004's coverage floor and FR-005's make entry point are kept over both crates.

decisions.summary: Every check in-process; one l7r-guard call per hook event.
decisions.why: Implements FR-007.

decisions.summary: Deciders run in today's settings order; refusals reported together, rewrites applied in order.
decisions.why: Makes the merged answer deterministic; serves FR-002's same-verdict rule.

decisions.summary: Dispatcher lands empty; each guard switches in its own commit removing its shell entry after its suite passes.
decisions.why: Implements FR-003 with the piece taken as one guard; no guard runs as both.

decisions.id: D4 - the suite is the replay
decisions.summary: tests/hooks/test-<guard>.sh runs against l7r-guard --only <guard>; unit tests beside the decider under 0.1 s each.
decisions.why: Implements FR-002's replay and FR-008. The suites staying shell is not Python; their inline Python is a separate matter (see P1-SCOPE).

decisions.summary: Guard log format, escape tokens, transcript and clone-map reads ported first as a shared library.
decisions.why: Keeps today's outputs (FR-002).

decisions.summary: A fact several deciders need is read once per process.
decisions.why: Carries FR-006's per-process design fixes.

decisions.id: D7 - binary from its own tree, failing open
decisions.summary: The wrapper builds the binary when sources are newer; a failure to build or run lets the call through with a notice and a guard-log line.
decisions.why: The request and spec say nothing on failure modes and no requirement is narrowed. Note: the justification that a crashing guard lets the call through today is stated, not measured, and one build failure now turns off all guards at once rather than one; that is design, not fidelity.

decisions.summary: pair-hooks, gate-hooks, measure-hooks, no-poll-hooks, main-tree-hooks, record-edit-hooks, then settings order.
decisions.why: Order of work inside phase 1; changes no scope.

decisions.summary: Scale/Scope states phase 1 is the 26 repository guards, their libraries and suites; the work breakdown (planned to the task) has no line for the inline Python sites in tests/hooks/ (and any non-guard Python in scripts/hooks/), keeps tests/hooks/hookdeps.py as Python rekeyed with no phase for its port, and item 7 only re-runs and records the census rather than requiring phase 1's share to return nothing.
decisions.why: FR-001 assigns to phase 1 every tracked .py under scripts/hooks/ and the libraries its guards call, every inline site in scripts/hooks/ AND tests/hooks/, and each tests/ file with the piece it tests. Nothing makes those impossible in phase 1; the narrowing is unlisted rather than argued, and it would reach ticked tasks. Fix: a work-breakdown line porting phase 1's inline sites (the suites' python3 -c and heredocs) and any remaining scripts/hooks/ Python; a stated phase and FR-001 basis for hookdeps.py (ported in phase 1, or named as the gate planner's in phase 2); item 7 to require phase 1's share of both censuses to return nothing.

decisions.summary: ci/, the gate's scripts, _invocation.py, switches.py and the gate recipes' inline Python; the Rust-only route lands early since it is most of SC-002.
decisions.why: Matches FR-001's phase-2 list and serves SC-002.

decisions.id: P3-SCOPE - tooling list omits the Makefile's other recipes
decisions.summary: Phase 3's approach names the rest of scripts/, tools/, pipeline/, helpers, specs/, recorded measurements and .specify/scripts/bash/ but not the inline Python of the Makefile's other recipes, which phase 2 explicitly does not claim; the shell scripts under specs/ are covered only by 'every file under specs/'.
decisions.why: FR-001 assigns the Makefile's other recipes and the shell scripts under specs/ to phase 3; as written those sites sit in no phase block. Lesser consequence than P1-SCOPE: phase 3 is approach-level, will be planned to the task and reviewed again, and SC-005's close would catch it - but it should be fixed in the same amendment by naming both in phase 3's approach.

decisions.id: P3 - tests rewritten as Rust, one end-to-end kept
decisions.summary: One crate a family of tools; each tool's tests rewritten in Rust, its one end-to-end test kept.
decisions.why: Implements FR-008 and FR-001's tests-with-their-piece rule.

decisions.summary: Mode A planner, pool generators, interactive/, then containers, lockfiles, pyproject tables and __init__.py last; close on SC-005.
decisions.why: Matches FR-001's phase-4 list and SC-005.

decisions.id: Bookends - phase not closed while its criterion is unmet
decisions.summary: No make perf bookends through phase 3; each phase re-runs its m: commands and is not closed while its success criterion is unmet; phase 4 takes bookends.
decisions.why: Implements FR-010 and is stricter than it; no map is rolled before phase 4.

decisions.id: Constitution X - discipline read for Rust
decisions.summary: Clippy pedantic, rustfmt, full coverage, red-green, function and file size limits; no overlap check added; remaining Python keeps clause 10's rules.
decisions.why: Holds FR-004 and keeps today's Rust crate rules; the request asks nothing about discipline changes.

decisions.id: Constitution XIV - two guards fixed in their port
decisions.summary: The make-only guard's pytest-in-grep misread and the guard-file guard's scratch-text misread are fixed as they move, case verdict changed and named in the same commit.
decisions.why: FR-002's own named exception, with its conditions repeated.

blocks: ### Phase 4 - Mode A and the page writer (Story 4, P4)

decisions.summary: One l7r-guard process per hook event, every check in-process
decisions.why: FR-007 (one process for a tool call); serves the GM's port of the hooks.

decisions.summary: Deciders run in today's settings order, rewrites seen by later deciders
decisions.why: Preserves today's merged answer, which FR-002 requires.

decisions.summary: Dispatcher lands empty; each guard moves in its own commit, shell entry removed with Rust decider added
decisions.why: FR-003: Python runs until the replacement passes, no piece runs both.

decisions.summary: The shell suite replayed against l7r-guard --only <guard> is the verdict replay; unit tests under 0.1 s
decisions.why: FR-002 (same verdicts on every suite case) and FR-008.

decisions.summary: Guard log format, escape tokens, transcript and clone-map reads ported first as a shared library
decisions.why: Keeps behavior identical (FR-002); ordering inside phase 1 is design.

decisions.summary: Facts several deciders need read once per process
decisions.why: FR-006 carries over 444 T36's read-once fixes.

decisions.summary: Wrapper builds from its own tree, keeps the last binary that passed --self-check, runs it on a failed build; fails open with notice and guard-log line only when no good binary was ever built
decisions.why: Does not relax FR-002: a crashing hook already passes today under Claude Code's non-blocking-error rule, and keeping the last good binary is stricter than that, so no case's verdict is weakened. The supporting claim that make land-tooling runs make hooks-test is a repository fact not checkable from the bundle; it is justification, not a decision.

decisions.summary: Guards ported by measured cost (pair, gate, measure, no-poll, main-tree, record-edit), then settings order
decisions.why: FR-001 orders the phases, not the guards inside phase 1.

decisions.summary: serde_json is the one external crate phase 1 adds; later crates named in each phase's amendment
decisions.why: Implementation choice; the request is the port, not a dependency rule.

decisions.summary: A Cargo workspace of crates by phase, rust/guard beside rust/phases
decisions.why: Structure of the Rust that replaces the Python; no request clause narrowed.

decisions.summary: scripts/hooks/lib/hm_*.py deleted as each last caller moves
decisions.why: FR-001 phase 1 (scripts/hooks/ and the libraries its guards call), deletion on switch per FR-003.

decisions.summary: tests/hooks/ 41 inline sites replaced as each suite is replayed; hookdeps/hooktrace/hookbench ported as l7r-guard subcommands, test_hooks_cases.py as crate tests
decisions.why: FR-001: each tests/ file goes with the piece it tests, and tests/hooks/ inline sites are phase 1. Closes the previous round's gap. Where the ported helpers live is design.

decisions.summary: Phase 1 close: m:hooks-bash and m:pair-hooks-suite re-run, phase 1's share of both censuses (every .py and inline site under scripts/hooks/ and tests/hooks/) empty, recorded
decisions.why: FR-001 (both censuses re-run at each phase end), FR-010, SC-001. The directory restatement of phase 1's share is faithful to FR-001's 'scripts/hooks/ and the libraries its guards call' provided m:guard-sources' 33 library files lie under scripts/hooks/, as Scale/Scope asserts ('everything FR-001 gives it'); any that lies elsewhere stays inside the feature (phase 3 takes the rest of scripts/, SC-005 empties both censuses), so nothing leaves the request - at most a file's phase shifts.

decisions.summary: Gate path (ci/, scripts/gates, scripts/measure, _invocation.py, switches.py, gate recipes' and named scripts' inline Python) to a Rust binary; Rust-only route early; planned to task when opened
decisions.why: Matches FR-001's phase 2 share item by item; deferral to a reviewed plan amendment is not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: Rest of scripts/, tools/, pipeline/, engine helpers, every .py and shell-inline Python under specs/, recorded Python measurements rewritten, Makefile's other recipes, .specify/scripts/bash/
decisions.why: Now carries every phase 3 item of both FR-001 censuses, including the Makefile's other recipes and specs/ shell scripts the previous round found missing.

decisions.summary: Mode A planner, pool/ generators, interactive/, then containers' Python, lockfile pairs, pyproject tables, __init__.py last; close is SC-005
decisions.why: Matches FR-001's phase 4 share and SC-005.

decisions.summary: No make perf bookends through phase 3; each phase measured against spec figures (FR-010); phase 4 takes bookends for Mode A sheets
decisions.why: No map is rolled before phase 4; FR-010's per-phase measurement is kept.

decisions.summary: Phase 1 planned to the task, phases 2-4 to approach, each amended and reviewed when it opens
decisions.why: Deferral with its own spec-fidelity review; nothing in the request or spec is dropped.

decisions.summary: Technical Context Scale/Scope: phase 1 is the 44 registered repository guards (m:registered-guards; 26 take a Bash call) plus everything FR-001 gives phase 1 (guard shell, their Python libraries, suite files and helpers, inline sites of scripts/hooks/ and tests/hooks/)
decisions.why: The change from '26 repository guards' to '44 registered' widens the stated phase-1 scope to every guard under scripts/hooks/, which is what FR-001 assigns to phase 1; the earlier figure counted only Bash-taking guards while the plan removed all 44 shell files. Re-ran m:registered-guards' command: 44, matching the 44 *-hooks.sh files.

decisions.summary: serde_json the one crate phase 1 adds; further crates named per phase
decisions.why: Unchanged from the CLEAR text; an implementation choice inside the request to make this a Rust codebase.

decisions.summary: A guard that cannot run fails open, saying so (R6)
decisions.why: Unchanged; matches Claude Code's existing behavior for a crashing hook and is bounded by D7's last-good-binary rule; previously judged CLEAR.

decisions.summary: One binary l7r-guard replaces the 44 registered guards, called once per hook event
decisions.why: Implements FR-001 phase 1 and FR-007; the count now covers every registered guard rather than 26, so no guard is left out of the port.

decisions.summary: One process, deciders as pure functions
Fixed order: today's settings order
decisions.why: Preserves today's verdicts (FR-002).

decisions.summary: Guard by guard, shell entry removed in the commit adding its decider
Existing suite is the replay; unit tests under 0.1 s each
Shared state (guard log, escapes, transcript, clone map) ported first as a library
decisions.why: Supports FR-002 parity.

decisions.summary: Facts read once per process
Binary built from its own tree, last good build kept, fail-open only with no good build ever
decisions.why: Unchanged and previously CLEAR; mechanism of running the replacement, not a narrowing of what is ported.

decisions.summary: Guards moved by measured cost first, then settings order; two over-refusing guards fixed as they move
decisions.why: Unchanged and previously CLEAR; ordering within phase 1 is left open by the spec.

decisions.summary: Work breakdown items 1-8 including the suites' Python, helpers ported to l7r-guard subcommands, and phase-1 share of both censuses returning nothing at close
decisions.why: Unchanged and previously CLEAR; item 8 enforces FR-001's per-phase census rerun.

decisions.summary: The Rust tools build as one cargo workspace (root rust/Cargo.toml naming phases and guard); rust_checks.py runs each member and skips the workspace's own manifest, which builds nothing.
decisions.why: Build layout for the port the GM asked for ('making this a Rust codebase'); the checks still cover every crate (FR-004) through make (FR-005). rust_checks.py staying Python for now is allowed by FR-003 and is itself in FR-001's census, so nothing is carved out.

decisions.summary: serde_json is the one crate added.
decisions.why: A dependency choice inside the port; it narrows nothing the request or spec asks for.

decisions.summary: The guard protocol and its merge of verdicts carried from D1, D2 and contracts/guard-protocol.md.
decisions.why: Implements FR-007 (one process per tool call) and FR-002 (same verdicts); no case of the hooks is excluded.

decisions.summary: The shared state is kept and the facts are asked once.
decisions.why: Carries the measured design fixes over as FR-006 requires; no behavior the GM asked to change is preserved by it.

decisions.summary: The wrapper keeps the last good binary.
decisions.why: A build-failure fallback to an earlier Rust binary, not a return to Python; it does not run a piece twice (FR-003) and does not exempt any piece from the port.

decisions.summary: The settings switch lands with an empty guard list, its own cost recorded as phase 1's floor.
decisions.why: FR-003 keeps the Python guards the ones that run until each replacement passes, so landing the switch with no guards moved is the ordering the spec requires; recording its cost serves FR-010 and SC-001.

decisions.summary: Landed via make land-tooling with no work budget; done is both crates' tests, lint, format, cover and dead clean through make.
decisions.why: Process and exit criteria that enforce FR-004 and FR-005; nothing narrowed.

decisions.summary: T002 builds the one-process hook dispatcher answering Claude Code's protocol with an empty guard list, guards ported later
decisions.why: A first step toward FR-007 (one process per tool call) inside FR-001's hooks-first phase; ports no guard, so FR-002/FR-003 are untouched (no Python replaced, none run twice).

decisions.summary: Done when an event with no guard allows in under a millisecond of its own work and every merge case passes; --self-check answers; coverage full
decisions.why: Acceptance targets that serve SC-001/FR-007 and FR-004's coverage floor; the millisecond is a target the plan sets for the empty dispatcher, not a measured figure, and drops nothing the request or spec asks.

decisions.summary: Every merge case in contracts/guard-protocol.md tested, each test under a tenth of a second
decisions.why: Restates FR-008 and the protocol contract; enforcement of what was asked.

decisions.summary: Runs after T001, lands via make land-tooling with no work budget; red exit records the failure, sets the task down, asks the arbiter
decisions.why: Sequencing and process; the GM's request (make this a Rust codebase) is unaffected, and FR-005 keeps make as the entry point.

decisions.summary: Build the shared state every guard reads (guard log, escapes, session clone and name, GM messages) as one library that reads each fact once and writes it in today's formats.
decisions.why: Serves the request's purpose (Python hooks too inefficient, port to Rust) and FR-007 (guards as one process); 'written as today' is FR-002's same-outputs rule. Nothing the request or spec asks is dropped. Note: the block's gloss of FR-006 as 'asked once, the count pinned' is a paraphrase - FR-006 names the import graph, semantic ids and the fixture; read-once shared state is in the same spirit, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: Green exit: a guard-log line written by Rust is read back by make guard-log exactly as the shell's is, and each read is counted once per process in a test.
decisions.why: Enforces FR-002 (same outputs) and the read-once design; verification of what was asked, not new scope.

decisions.summary: Red exit: record what failed, set the task down, route a process stop to make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: Process routing; neither narrows nor extends the request.

decisions.summary: Runs after T002; lands via make land-tooling with no work budget; no researched value or constant moves.
decisions.why: Ordering and landing mechanics inside the hooks phase (FR-001's phase order); no requirement is relaxed.

decisions.summary: Done = the library's tests green and its reads counted.
decisions.why: Does not exempt the library from FR-004 (coverage floor) or FR-008 (test time), which still bind every replacement; the checklist omits restating them rather than carving them out.

blocks: ### T006-T049 - one task a guard (phase 1, work breakdown 5, 7)
### T050-T052 - the suites' tooling and the close (phase 1, work breakdown 6-8)

decisions.summary: Technical Context: Rust edition 2021 on the toolchain rust/phases builds with; a Cargo workspace, phase 1's crate rust/guard with binary l7r-guard; storage files only, as today
decisions.why: Unchanged from the CLEAR text apart from the crate line; the request is to make this a Rust codebase and these choices do not narrow it.

decisions.summary: fancy-regex added as the second external crate so the guards' patterns that use lookaround or backreferences can be carried over verbatim; hm_shape.py (heredoc and quote stripping) ported in T003 with it
decisions.why: A dependency choice serving FR-002 (same verdicts) and FR-001 (every Python file replaced by Rust); it narrows nothing the GM asked. The ruling does not depend on the count of 43 (research R8, 2026-11-07, not re-runnable from this bundle): one lookaround pattern would be enough to need the crate to keep the patterns verbatim. What actually holds FR-002 is the per-guard suite replay (D4) going green, not the Complexity row's premise that a verbatim pattern gives identical verdicts - Python re and fancy-regex differ at edges ($ before a trailing newline, Unicode \d/\w, \Z).

decisions.summary: A hand-written matcher in place of a fancy-regex pattern only where a profile shows that pattern hot, decided in its guard's task
decisions.why: A design default inside the request; the verdicts stay bound by FR-002 and its suite either way.

decisions.summary: serde_json for the protocol; the wrapper keeps the last good binary and fails open only when none was ever built (D7, R6)
decisions.why: Text carried from blocks judged CLEAR; unchanged in substance.

decisions.summary: Workspace root rust/Cargo.toml naming phases and guard; protocol and merge (D1, D2); shared state and facts asked once (D5, D6, T003); wrapper keeping the last good binary (T004); settings switch landed with an empty guard list, the dispatcher called once an event beside the shell guards it does not yet hold, its floor timed (T005)
decisions.why: The transitional coexistence keeps FR-003 (no guard runs twice) and works toward FR-007; nothing asked is dropped. Carried from the CLEAR range block plus the fancy-regex line judged above.

decisions.summary: One task a guard: the Rust guard registered, the shell and its settings entry removed in the same commit (D3, FR-003); the guard's suite as its verdict replay, its inline Python replaced in the same task (D4); order by measured cost first (R2); each task landed with make land-tooling
decisions.why: Applies FR-001, FR-002 and FR-003 guard by guard; the order and the landing route narrow nothing. The 44 tasks T006-T049 match the 44 registered guards in Technical Context. FR-002's 'every case its tests and its suites hold' still binds each task: the Done line names the suite, and any other test of the same guard's cases is not displaced by it.

decisions.id: T028 / T029 / T006-T049 range: XIV fixes
decisions.summary: Two constitution XIV fixes, on make-only-hooks and guard-file-hooks, taken under FR-002's exception; the template line 'XIV's fix named' on the other guard blocks
decisions.why: FR-002 itself provides this exception (a guard that refuses correct work today is fixed in its port, its expected verdict changed, the change named in the commit and the phase's record). The range block names exactly two guards; each fix's legitimacy is for its own task, where the case and the change are visible. The template line on the other 42 blocks grants no further license, since FR-002 already conditions the exception on the guard refusing correct work today. T028/T029 say 'named in its task'; FR-002's 'named in the commit and in the phase's record' still binds and the Done line does not displace it.

decisions.summary: The four tests/hooks Python helpers (hookbench, hookdeps, hooktrace, test_hooks_cases) ported as l7r-guard subcommands and crate tests; done when no .py remains under tests/hooks/
decisions.why: FR-001 puts each tests/ file with the piece it tests; FR-008 applies. The Done line is narrower than FR-001's recorded-measurement clause, which binds this commit: every specs/*/measurements*.json command that runs one of these helpers (m:hooks-bash and m:pair-hooks-suite, which T052 re-runs, plausibly among them) is rewritten in the commit that ports it and re-run as its proof. The clause still binds; the Done line does not displace it.

decisions.summary: Each guard library deleted with its last caller; done when no .py and no inline Python remain under scripts/hooks/, make audit and make guard-log reading the Rust lines unchanged
decisions.why: Porting a library nothing calls would be unrequested scope; deleting it with its last caller completes FR-001 for phase 1. As with T050, FR-001's recorded-measurement rewrite binds the commits that port or delete these files (T003 included); the Done line does not displace it.

decisions.summary: Phase 1 closed: figures re-run and recorded beside their first values, SC-001 met, both censuses' phase-1 share empty
decisions.why: FR-010 (timings measured against the spec's figures) and FR-001 (both censuses re-run at the phase's end) applied to phase 1; SC-002 and SC-003 belong to later phases and the feature's close. FR-010's 'recorded in dev/' and FR-002's 'named in the phase's record' for the two XIV fixes still bind this close; the Done line does not displace them.

decisions.summary: With no good binary ever built, the wrapper lets the call through with a notice and a guard-log line
decisions.why: This is plan D7's own outcome, not new in this block. It is held against FR-002, which asks for the same verdicts on every case the tests and suites hold. Having no binary at all is not one of those cases. The case that matches it today is a guard whose Python cannot start, and m:python-dead-fails-open measures that this already fails open (repo-safety exits 0 on a force push to main, make-only prints nothing, gate exits 127). So no verdict gets weaker than today's. Making it fail closed would be new behavior the GM did not ask for. The earlier BLOCKED version justified this from FR-005's make-only clause. The block now cites the requirement that actually governs verdicts.

decisions.summary: A failed build (does not compile, or compiles and fails l7r-guard --self-check) runs the last good binary; a stale build is rebuilt
decisions.why: This repeats D7 word for word, and the self-check is D7's own definition of a good build. Today a broken Python guard crashes and fails open, so keeping the previous guards running gives a verdict no weaker than today's. The request asks for a port and nothing here cuts what it covers.

decisions.summary: T004 replaces no guard; T005 adds the wrapper to the settings with an empty guard list; each guard task moves one decider in and removes that guard's shell script and settings entry in the same landing
decisions.why: This is how the plan carries out FR-003: the Python stays the one that runs until its replacement passes, and no piece runs in both. Separate processes for the guards still being moved are a temporary state. FR-007's one process is where the work ends up, and this order does not give it up.

decisions.summary: FR-005's clause that the make-only guard must cover the replacements' binaries is left to T028, not this task
decisions.why: This assigns the requirement to another task and narrows nothing. The clause is about the make-only guard's coverage, not about the wrapper. FR-005 still applies to the feature in full, and the block names the task that carries it.

decisions.summary: Lands through make land-tooling with no work budget and nothing rolled; no researched value or constant moves
decisions.why: This is process and tooling scope only. Nothing the GM asked for is changed.

decisions.summary: Every session's settings call the one dispatcher once per event, beside the Python guards it does not yet hold.
decisions.why: FR-001 ports the hooks first and FR-003 requires each unported guard's Python to stay the one that runs while no guard runs twice; FR-007's single process is the end state reached as pieces move in. A coexistence period is what FR-003 itself describes, not a carve-out from the GM's request to make this a Rust codebase.

decisions.summary: After T004; landed alone with make land-tooling.
decisions.why: Sequencing and landing route only; the spec leaves both open and neither narrows what is ported.

decisions.summary: Green: settings call it for every event, make hooks-test green, its floor timed. Red: failure recorded, task set down, process stop to make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: The green exit enforces FR-002/FR-003 (hooks-test) and FR-010 (timed); the red exit stops rather than relaxing any requirement.

decisions.summary: No work budget, nothing rolled, for a tooling landing.
decisions.why: Process bookkeeping; it changes nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: Re-run m:hooks-bash's command with the dispatcher in place and record the floor.
decisions.why: Serves FR-010 and SC-001's measurement against m:hooks-bash; it does not claim SC-001 met or move its target.

decisions.id: T005-6 no constant or room question
decisions.summary: No researched value moves; no constant moved; not a room question.
decisions.why: Statements that the task touches only Claude Code tool-call guards, consistent with FR-009's scope and the request.

decisions.summary: Shared facts (guard log, escapes, clone/name, GM messages) read once per process, counts pinned in a test; hm_shape heredoc/quote stripping ported with fancy-regex
decisions.why: Unchanged from its CLEAR reading; carries FR-002, FR-006 and plan D5-D6, part of porting the hooks (phase 1 of the GM's 'making this a Rust codebase').

decisions.summary: Every specs/*/measurements*.json command that runs a file the task ports or deletes is rewritten to the port in the same commit and re-run as proof
decisions.why: The added sentence restates FR-001's recorded-measurement clause (rewritten in the commit that ports what it runs, re-run as the proof) at the tasks that port or delete Python; it narrows nothing and enforces the accepted spec.

decisions.summary: make-only-hooks port gains suite cases refusing a direct Bash run of a replacement's binary (l7r-guard, hamlet, from the cargo target dir or by path) with the make target that runs it
decisions.why: FR-005 requires the make-only guard to cover the replacements' binaries as it covers Python and cargo today; the new cases are the test that enforces that requirement, at the task that ports that guard.

decisions.summary: Each guard's constitution XIV fix named in its commit and in the phase's record (was: 'in its task')
decisions.why: Brings the block into line with FR-002's exception wording (named in the commit and in the phase's record); the XIV exception itself is the spec's, not a new carve-out by the plan.

decisions.summary: guard-file-hooks verdicts given by the Rust guard via its suite replay, shell and settings entry removed in the registering commit
decisions.why: Unchanged apart from the XIV wording; carries FR-002, FR-003, FR-008, D3-D4.

decisions.summary: tests/hooks Python helpers (the four in m:guard-sources) ported, make hooks-test keyed by l7r-guard deps, no .py under tests/hooks/
decisions.why: FR-001 places tests/hooks/ Python in phase 1; only the FR-001 measurement-rewrite sentence was added.

decisions.summary: No guard library outlives its last caller; no .py and no inline Python under scripts/hooks/
decisions.why: FR-001 census and second census for scripts/hooks/ in phase 1; only the FR-001 measurement-rewrite sentence was added.

decisions.summary: Phase 1 closes with SC-001 met, both censuses' phase-1 share empty, the phase's measurements recorded in dev/ as well as beside their first values, and the record naming the two XIV fixes
decisions.why: The additions are FR-010 (timings recorded in dev/) and FR-002 (the XIV changes named in the phase's record), both requirements of the accepted spec; nothing is dropped from the earlier CLEAR text.

decisions.summary: serde_json as the first external crate
decisions.why: Unchanged; an implementation choice inside the port the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: fancy-regex as the second crate for the guards' lookaround/backreference patterns, its verdicts proven by each guard's suite replay (FR-002, D4) rather than asserted
decisions.why: The change cites m:guard-regex-features and replaces 'so verdicts stay the same' with the suite replay as proof, which is FR-002 and D4; it narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: A failed build runs the last good binary; fail open only when no good binary was ever built
